decisions.text: type arrow: two periods: the change between them is the point (06 DP6-3, G1.46): the default is an arrow chart, each category's change in units and in % side by side (G1.47), or a chart of the change itself (the % panel alone, facts.message relative_change; or the change as bars, a previous_period comparison with transform deviation); clustered bars of the two periods only where each period's own values, not the change, are what the request needs: facts.message periods, with the reason, grounded in the request, in reasons["facts.message"]
the values are not far from zero compared with their spread
two panels sharing the rows: the values, before to after; the change in %, from 0 % (G1.47, G7.21)
rows by the before value, largest first
no good or bad reading is given (measure.good): rises in the first palette colour, falls in the second, never red and green (G7.22, D-40)
the % panel: −20–50 by 10, holding 0 %, where its arrows start
the % panel's labels would crowd in its width: −20–60 by 20
the values in the measure's unit, 0–600 by 100, each arrow from before to after; the scale's title below: “Donations ($K)”
the change in %, −20–60 by 20, each arrow from 0 %; the scale's title below: “Change in donations”
an arrow chart (G7.21): a dot at the start, a shaft, a head whose tip sits exactly on the end value; one row per category, its name at the left

changes shorter than a full head with its start dot, their direction kept readable (--arrow-short-head: fit): the head shrunk to fit between the start dot and the end: East (values); the head over the start dot, haloed: West (values)
the key “Before blitz” and “After blitz” beside the ends of South's arrow, the longest, too short to hold both words over it (G7.21)
the title wraps onto two lines

source.shows: a look-up version with no good or bad reading declared: rises in the palette's first colour and falls in its second, never red and green (G7.22, D-40)

path.text: arrow charts may be new to a general audience: teach them (build the chart up, show first the familiar chart that fails, or add two or three callouts stating the obvious; G1.5), or state the insight in a sentence and keep the chart as backup (G1.6)
